# 9 Bounceback Candidates For The 2026/27 NBA Season

Locked On Fantasy Basketball, 2026-07-20, 30:50. https://youtu.be/-KS_AZjZnw4

## Summary

Josh Lloyd covers nine bounceback candidates for the 2026/27 season. His case is that players who struggled last season often did so for specific, fixable reasons: injuries, low minutes, a bad role or team environment, and free throw drops with no clear cause. His candidates are Coby White, Jalen Green, Myles Turner, Trae Young, John Collins, Zach LaVine, Domantas Sabonis, Ivica Zubac and Jalen Williams. He warns that drafting straight off last season's rankings means passing on players who should rebound and reaching for players who sit high in the rankings. His price targets: Turner around the top 60, Young possibly top 20 if he goes in the 40s, Zubac in the 80s or 90s, and Williams in the top 50 but not in rounds two or three. At the end he names a few more possible bouncebacks: Cam Thomas, Nick Richards, Nikola Vucevic, Bol Bol and Darius Bazley.

## Rules and methods

- [4:44](https://youtu.be/-KS_AZjZnw4?t=284) Do not draft straight off last season's rankings. You will miss the players you should jump to grab and take players everyone else avoids too early because they sit high in the rankings.
  > "And the players who everyone's avoiding, you'll grab too early because they're sitting at the top of the rankings"
- [4:35](https://youtu.be/-KS_AZjZnw4?t=275) Some people say projections are pointless and you can just draft from last season's rankings. The speaker disagrees.
  > "Just look at the rankings from last season and if you draft from there, you'll be fine."
- [2:56](https://youtu.be/-KS_AZjZnw4?t=176) Bounceback candidates come partly from role changes, and partly from injuries and shooting slumps.
  > "when we talk about bounceback candidates for this season, some of it is role based."
- [6:26](https://youtu.be/-KS_AZjZnw4?t=386) Injuries have a hidden cost. Besides the missed games, a player stays on limited minutes while ramping back up, so all of his numbers drop.
  > "that's the hidden impact of um injuries is not only does it mean he only played 32 games"
- [17:51](https://youtu.be/-KS_AZjZnw4?t=1071) Several players had big free throw drops for no clear reason. Treat that as a pattern that likely reverts.
  > "Are you seeing a common pattern here? Why did he go from an 85% free throw guy to a 77?"
- [27:36](https://youtu.be/-KS_AZjZnw4?t=1656) Check the context behind numbers. Stats a wing piled up while playing center may not hold when he moves back to his normal position on a healthy team.
  > "you always have to be careful of it where he had those high block rates, high rebound rates, high field goal percentage rates"
- [21:36](https://youtu.be/-KS_AZjZnw4?t=1296) Under the new tanking rules, teams get no real benefit from sitting players late in the season.
  > "And we all know that with the tanking rules in place, there's no real benefit from teams having to sit guys down."
- [22:01](https://youtu.be/-KS_AZjZnw4?t=1321) Teams that do not control their own draft picks have no reason to finish bottom three, so they keep pushing to win.
  > "But those teams that don't have control of their draft picks, there's no benefit for them to finish in the bottom three."
- [12:49](https://youtu.be/-KS_AZjZnw4?t=769) Past high rankings can be misleading. Turner's top 20 finish was a flaw in the rankings, and Zubac's 9-cat rank did not reflect his real value.
  > "when he was a top 20 player, he really wasn't. That was a rankings flaw."
